data.content_ref: inline:The 'Justification Trace' criterion cannot distinguish genuine reliability from compliance when the panel has been trained to produce justifications. The problem explicitly asks for evidence that separates genuine gain from 'checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer.' If a panel is trained to cite case-specific evidence for each item — a learned discursive template — their justifications will look evidentiary yet remain rote compliance. The target's own countercondition ('trained to hallucinate justifications') is acknowledged but never resolved: the proposed trace would misclassify such a panel as genuinely reliable.
